fixtureProvenance.note: Authored from scratch for issue #508. Not reused from examples/pipeline-benchmark/corpus/ (real third-party pages, vendored under issue #315's distinct, narrower accepted-risk posture, not for this public example gallery) or from any other corpus in this repository.

commandNote.note: route-metadata (source/effects/metadata_route_cli.d) is dispatched directly from source/cli_commands.d's runCommands() before argparse's generic parse, and its own parseOptions() recognizes only --input/--content-output/--metadata-output/--manifest/--filters/--retry -- there is no --config flag and no JSON-loading code path anywhere in metadata_route_cli.d. This is a real, current limitation of the command itself, not a gap in this example: route-metadata has a CLI-flag form only. This example instead proves CLI-token determinism by running the identical command twice, as two separate real process invocations against the same --input path, and diffing both sinks byte-for-byte.

artifacts.expectedOutcome: Synthetic HTML dispatch note carrying a real title/author/date/url/site-name/description metadata block, plus a CRLF and a lone-CR line ending in its body text so route-metadata's default content filters (normalize-line-endings, strip-control) do real, visible work rather than a no-op pass-through.

artifacts.provenance: Generated from the authored issue #508 input by the shipping scrubbed binary for this checked-in golden corpus.
artifacts.expectedOutcome: The content sink: byte-identical to the input except every CRLF/lone-CR line ending normalized to a single LF (normalize-line-endings); no control bytes were present to strip. HTML markup, attributes, and all metadata-bearing tags pass through completely unmodified -- route-metadata's content filters never parse or alter HTML structure.

artifacts.expectedOutcome: The metadata sink: a document-metadata:v1 wire record with the run's own doc:v1:sha256(...) document_id (deterministic per the local --input absolute path, not per content -- see domain.document.DocumentId.from) replaced by the literal token <DOCUMENT_ID>, and the four standard fields (title, author, date, url) plus two extension fields (site-name, description) selected from the input's metadata markup. Every field other than documentId is fully content-deterministic and diffed exactly.
